title: Simply Majestic
reviewNotes: Three selected branches, 19 exact positions from the complete six-piece source root. Bh6+ preserves the g-pawn; g8=Q+ ...Kxg8 Ke6 creates a cage, then ...Kh8 Kf7 ...e5 Bg7# is actual mate. Immediate gxh7 ...Kg7 h8=Q+ ...Kxh8 draws. The selected ...e5 alternative preserves White’s win and stops before assuming an unencoded bishop conversion.
transcript: A wise man once said that if something feels off, chances are something is. White has a bishop for a pawn. And so it would feel natural that white is winning in this position. But if we pay closer attention, we're going to notice that there is a problem. There is a tension between these two pawns. And if the white pawn is somehow traded off, this is simply going to be a draw. There is no way to win with just a bishop left. But unfortunately, if you take the black pawn now, this is simply going to be a draw. After king to G7, the king attacks the pawn. you cannot promote it. You're simply going to lose the new queen. And there is no way to defend this pawn, which means that black is going to be able to pick it up and secure a draw. But some of you might notice that white has the chance to play bishop to H6, now giving a check and forcing the black king to move. If the king steps away, this is an easy win. We're simply taking the pawn. But if the king goes to G8, now we have to save the pawn with G7. We cannot allow black to trade it off. And now we're at a crossroads. Black only has two choices. To either push the pawn or to walk out with the king. Pushing the pawn would make no sense because after king to E6, now the black king is stuck inside this cage. The pawn has to push and we're going to collect it with the bishop, allowing this other pawn to move. And this is going to be an easy win. But of course, black can simply go to f7. And now it might seem like he is simply out of the woods. There is no way to make progress in this position. The white king cannot really come to help the pawn and the bishop can never defend the promotion square. But white has a brilliant little trick in this position. And the trick is to promote to a queen. And some of you might think, well, this doesn't make any sense. The king is simply going to take the queen. And you told us that a bishop alone is not going to be able to checkmate the black king. But you would be mistaken because after king to E6, we are now blocking both of the black pawns and making sure that the king cannot come out in the open. Meaning that black is in zukswang. The only move that could secure a draw for him is to stay exactly where he is. But of course, he has to move. And so he will move to the corner. But now after king to F7, the black pawn is free to move. And white is going to win with bishop to G7 checkmate.
